description: Writes and sends an email to someone, and opens the thread their answer will land in. The text goes out as given, so this is the tool for a message a person has read and approved. With "send_at" it is scheduled instead: nothing leaves until then, and list_scheduled_sends shows it waiting.

attachments.description: Files to send along, up to 10 and 7 MiB in total. Each one is named EITHER by "upload_id", a file already pushed to a slot from create_attachment_upload, OR inline by "filename" and "content_base64". Prefer the upload for anything but a few lines of text: a file written out as base64 has to be produced character by character, which a real document overruns long before the 7 MiB cap.

content_base64.description: The file itself, base64 encoded. Inline form only, and only worth it for something small.

content_type.description: The media type, for example "application/pdf". Derived from the name when left out.

filename.description: The name the recipient sees, extension included. Inline form only.

upload_id.description: A file already sent to its upload address, as create_attachment_upload gives it. The other fields are then left out: the name and the media type are the ones the slot was opened with.

bcc.description: Who else receives it without the others being told. A blind copy is kept on the sending alone: the thread records the visible recipients only.

body.description: The text of the message, as the contact will read it. Plain text, in their language.

cc.description: Who else receives it, in copy. Everyone on the mail sees these.

contact_name.description: The name of the recipient, recorded on their fiche when we open one.

from.description: The address to send from: one of the account inbound addresses, or one of the other names of a mailbox, which is what brings the answer back into that mailbox. Call list_sender_addresses to find them, aliases included.

send_at.description: When it should leave, if not now: a date and time with its offset, such as "2026-10-12T08:30:00+03:00", at most a year ahead. Without an offset it is read in the zone of the person this connection acts for. Left out, it leaves at once.

subject.description: The subject line, up to 255 characters.

to.description: Who it is written to. The thread is filed under the first of them.

name: send_email
title: Send a new email
